title: Stop calling merge targets thieves, and retire 30 synonyms that name other compounds (#669)
body:
Addresses #669 (115 → 59 baselined pairs) and fixes #698's rename path.

Rule K (#670) baselined 115 pairs where a row's `other` carried a name another record owns. Cleaning them meant asking *why* each was there. Three different answers came back.

## 1. 54 were never violations — my own rule was wrong

Rule K's ownership map read every file under `mapped/` without checking `mapping_status`. A `REJECTED` record there is a **merge tombstone**: 62 of the 63 in the corpus carry a MERGE-type event, and the last is an explicit `REPOINTED_TOMBSTONE_IDENTIFIER`. The merge moved the name to the target, so `MIM:Acetate` carrying `Acetate (carbon source)` is the rightful holder, not a thief.

Tombstones no longer own names. 51 false positives and 3 already-stale entries leave the baseline, and a new test refuses any baseline entry that matches no live violation — so it can only shrink honestly.

## 2. 40 of the remaining 61 are a harmless round trip

They arrive from kg-microbe's synonyms for the *shared ontology object*. Downstream they re-attach to that same object. Ugly in this file, harmless in the graph. Left baselined.

## 3. The other 21 are where the real problem was

`Ca(NO3)2` is **calcium** nitrate (`CHEBI:64205`). It was once mis-mapped to **cadmium** nitrate; the mapping was corrected, and the six synonyms harvested while it was wrong stayed behind. They publish through `other` on an `exactMatch` row, which kg-microbe merges into the object's synonym set.

In the label index CultureMech consumes:

```
-Cadmium(II) nitrate,synonym,CHEBI:64205,Ca(NO3)2,…,MAPPED,unique
-arsenite,synonym,CHEBI:29125,Arsenate,…,MAPPED,unique
```

Resolved **uniquely** — not even flagged ambiguous. Rule K saw one of the six, because only one happens to be another record's preferred_term.

So the sweep is by **ChEBI's own name lists**, not by Rule K: a synonym ChEBI gives to a different term and does *not* give to the record's own.

| record | carried names of | n |
|---|---|---:|
| Ca(NO3)2 *calcium nitrate* | **cadmium nitrate** | 6 |
| Arsenate | **arsenite(1−)** — different oxidation state | 6 |
| Lithocholic acid | tricine, berbaman | 4 |
| Thiamine pyrophosphate | **pyrithiamine pyrophosphate** — its antagonist | 3 |
| Na2S2O3 | nonaethylene glycol monomethyl ether | 3 |
| 3-Indolyl acetic acid / 4-Hydroxyphenyl acetic acid / DL-Malic acid | ethyl 2-hexenoate / aspyrone / garciniaxanthone F | 2 each |
| Phenyl acetic acid / Trisodium citrate | LSM-15166 / citric acid | 1 each |

**30 on 10 records.** Each (own, wrong) pair checked by hand: no ChEBI edge joins the two in either direction, and their InChIKey connectivity differs. Related forms — paraquat and its dichloride, a stereoisomer and its racemate — show a `has_part` edge or a shared skeleton, are a curator's call, and are **not** touched.

Marked `REJECTED_LABEL`, not deleted. The provenance is real, and claw's builder filters *every* candidate alternate — kg-microbe's included — through the record's rejected labels, so the tombstone keeps a name out even while kg-microbe still supplies it. Deletion would let the next rebuild restore it. All ten `other` cells match what claw's merged builder produces.

Twelve of the thirty carry the source `sssom_other_backfill` — a backfill copied SSSOM `other` tokens *back* into curated YAML, round-tripping kg-microbe's contamination into MIM's records.

## 4. Doing this by the book exposed a defect in the book — #698

`save_yaml` backs a file up into a **gitignored** `backups/` directory beside it. The exporter's filename index enumerated with `rglob`, so every edited record appeared twice, both continuity keys collided, `for_record` returned `None`, and **`just sync-curated` renamed the records that had just been edited**.

| checkout | records with no filename continuity |
|---|---:|
| pristine `main` | 0 |
| after this ten-record edit | **21 — 8 of them published SSSOM subjects** |

On macOS git cannot see it (`core.ignorecase`), but a local claw rebuild published `MIM:Ca_NO32` for `MIM:Ca_No32`. On a case-sensitive filesystem it strands the subject outright — the #236/#300 failure, arriving through the filesystem.

`iter_record_files()` now enumerates the way `aggregate_records` does. With 11 backups present, `sync-curated` re-cases **0** files, down from 8. My own freshness gate from #653 had the same `rglob` and takes the same fix. No field was lost on the ten records — checked key by key.

## Verification

Mutation-checked: restoring the `rglob` fails 3 tests; letting tombstones own names again fails 2.

| gate | result |
|---|---|
| `validate-all` / `qc-sssom` (A–L) / `qc-roundtrip` / `qc-flat-coverage` / `check-unified-freshness` | pass |
| `lint` / `format-check` / `typecheck` / `check-instruction-refs` | clean |

`sync-curated` also corrected `mapped_count`, already stale on `main` (2618 declared, 2616 actual). No record's status moved here.
